idiom_name: class static field behind instance accessors (private #field)
implementation_notes: JavaScript keeps the state on the constructor rather than on the instance: a static field is created once on the class (a private #-field keeps it encapsulated) and instance methods read it through the class name, while static properties exist precisely for caches, fixed configuration and other data that must not be replicated across instances. What replaces the classic structure is the static keyword plus ES2022 static class fields, which make the slot part of the class definition instead of being bolted on in module scope. Prefer this form when the type must stay a real class (inheritance, private brand checks).
pitfalls: Static state is per module copy in the realm: duplicated bundles, workers, vm contexts and test module resets each load their own class, so the sharing never crosses realms or threads.

Static lookup goes through the prototype chain: a subclass that declares its own static field shadows the parent's slot silently, and this.constructor.state in an instance method may resolve to the subclass.
Module-level state survives between tests in the same process; without an explicit reset the second test inherits the first test's data.

variants.name: Factory closure over module-scope state
variants.idiom_name: factory function closing over a module-scope state cell
variants.implementation_notes: Before static class fields (or when the instances should be plain objects rather than class instances), the same behaviour comes from a factory closing over module-scope state: the module is evaluated once, so every object the factory returns shares the closed-over cell while each object keeps its own identity. This is the module-pattern form of shared state, and it needs no class machinery; use it when the shared state is an implementation detail rather than part of a type's static surface.
pitfalls: Declaring the state inside the factory gives every object its own copy - the closure must be created once, outside the factory, or the pattern silently becomes per-instance.
The sharing has no static surface at all, so it cannot be reset from outside except through the exported API; keep a reset function next to the factory for tests.
Two loaded copies of the module (bundler duplication, worker threads) create two independent cells.
